standard_prerequisites.name: The inverse system of powers I^n is pro-isomorphic to the system generated by the n-th powers of a finite set of generators, and the auxiliary systems attached to the generators carry the same pro-information
standard_prerequisites.use: Replaces the original system by the system generated by the chosen generators and reduces the statement to that system.

standard_prerequisites.name: An isomorphism of pro-objects of a derived category can be checked on cohomology in each degree, and it suffices to compute the derived tensor product with a bounded above complex of finite free modules in place of the bounded complex M
standard_prerequisites.use: Reduces the pro-isomorphism of complexes to a pro-isomorphism of modules in each cohomological degree, for a convenient representative of M.

standard_prerequisites.name: The Artin-Rees consequence supplies the pro-isomorphism between the cohomology of the tensor product with the powers of the generators and the cohomology of the ordinary products
standard_prerequisites.use: Provides the final pro-isomorphism, thereby proving the lemma.

core_obligations: Choose generators f_1, ..., f_r of I, record that the inverse system of powers of I is pro-isomorphic to the system generated by the n-th powers of the generators, and reduce the statement to the corresponding system of maps (proof lines 29687-29698).

Suppose M vanishes outside an interval from a to b and observe that both source and target of the reduced system have cohomology only in degrees between -r + a and b, so that it suffices to prove the pro-isomorphism for the induced system on cohomology in an arbitrary degree (proof lines 29699-29710).

Use the pro-isomorphisms available between the systems attached to the generators and the original systems of powers to replace the systems on both sides by the versions built from I^n, and then choose a bounded above complex P of finite free modules with a quasi-isomorphism to M so that it suffices to compare the cohomology of the tensor product with the ordinary products for P (proof lines 29711-29730).
Conclude with the Artin-Rees consequence, which states exactly that the last comparison is a pro-isomorphism because the cohomology of P and of M agree (proof lines 29731-29733).
proof_roadmap: Replace the system of powers of I by the system generated by finitely many chosen generators and reduce to the corresponding system of maps (proof lines 29687-29698).
Bound the cohomological degrees and reduce to a pro-isomorphism in each single degree by the criterion for pro-isomorphisms (proof lines 29699-29710).
Replace M by a bounded above complex of finite free modules and rewrite both sides in terms of the powers of the ideal (proof lines 29711-29730).
Invoke the Artin-Rees consequence to finish (proof lines 29731-29733).
difficulty_reason: The statement says that for a Noetherian ring A, an ideal I and a bounded complex M of finite modules, the inverse system of comparison maps from the derived tensor product of I^n with M to the ordinary products I^n M is an isomorphism of pro-objects of the derived category (statement lines 29676-29685). The proof is a chain of three reductions, each of which has to be justified: the passage from the powers of the ideal to the system generated by finitely many chosen generators, the passage from an isomorphism of pro-objects of complexes to pro-isomorphisms on cohomology in each degree, and the replacement of M by a bounded above complex of finite free modules; only then does the Artin-Rees consequence apply (proof lines 29687-29733). The degree bound on the two systems, which comes from the number of generators, is what makes the second reduction legitimate. The counted span refers three times to results of this chapter, one of them after the reduction, all carried as navigation stubs.
